journey.name: TL-09 A second delete does not replace the first undo offer
journey.description:
REGRESSION GUARD. This journey used to assert the defect: `TaskListUiState` held one nullable `message`, so a second delete overwrote the first `TaskDeleted` before the user could act on it and the first task became unrecoverable. Fixed alongside issue #15 - the state now holds a queue and nothing may displace an offer that has not been acted on.
Both offers are honoured, in the order they were made. The snackbar text is the same for either, so the guarantee being pinned here is that two rapid deletes cost the user nothing: the first Undo restores the first deleted task, and the second offer is still waiting behind it.
Restored tasks come back at the bottom with new ids, which is TL-06's finding and expected here.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Renew domain registration" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Immediately tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Reply to design feedback" row
Verify that both rows are gone and exactly two elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" with an "Undo" action is still on screen
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Renew domain registration" is on screen again, as the offer made first
Verify that a second message reading "Task deleted" with an "Undo" action is now on screen
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Reply to design feedback" is on screen again
Verify that exactly four elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
